cloudflare: Use the link here to open the token page with two permissions filled in, Zone > DNS > Edit and Zone > Zone > Read; add them yourself if they are missing.
Limit the token to the one zone you use here, not all zones.
Do not set "Token expiration" or "Client IP Address Filtering": the node keeps using this token and its address can change.
Choose "Continue to summary" and "Create Token", then copy the token; it is shown only once.
godaddy: Sign in at developer.godaddy.com/personal-access-token and choose "Generate Token".
Under "Permissions", expand "Domains & DNS" and select only domains.domain:read and domains.dns:update.
Set "Expires After" to 1 year, the longest choice, and replace the token before that date.
Choose "Create Token" and "Copy Token"; it is shown only once.
route53: In Route 53, open your hosted zone and copy its hosted zone ID.
In IAM, choose "Policies" > "Create policy" > "JSON" and paste the policy from doc/user/dns-providers/route53.md in the BuckyOS repository; it allows only this zone and the names BuckyOS writes.
Create an IAM user without console access and attach that policy.
Open the user, then "Security credentials" > "Create access key" > "Other", and copy both values; the secret access key is shown only once.
porkbun: Open "ACCOUNT" > "API Access", enter a title, and choose the permission "Manage, but no purchases".
Limit the key to your domain, and leave the IP addresses empty because the node's address can change.
Choose "Create API Key" and copy the API Key and the Secret Key; the Secret Key is shown only once.
Open "ACCOUNT" > "Domain Management", choose "Details" next to the domain, and turn on "API Access".
ionos: The first time, sign up for API access at my.ionos.com/shop/product/ionos-api (use the IONOS site of your country).
Open developer.hosting.ionos.com/keys and choose "Create New Key".
Copy the Public Prefix and the Secret and enter them joined by a dot (prefix.secret); the Secret is shown only once.
ovh: Open the key page of your region and sign in: auth.eu.ovhcloud.com/api/createToken (Europe), auth.ca.ovhcloud.com/api/createToken (Canada and Asia-Pacific) or auth.us.ovhcloud.com/api/createToken (United States).
Set "Validity" to "Unlimited" and do not restrict IP addresses.
Under "Rights", add GET, POST, PUT and DELETE for /domain/zone/example.com/*, with your own domain instead of example.com.
Choose "Create keys" and copy the application key, application secret and consumer key.
hetzner: Open console.hetzner.com and the project that holds the domain's DNS zone; tokens of the old DNS Console no longer work.
Open "Security" > "API tokens" > "Generate API token" and choose "Read & Write".
Copy the token; it cannot be shown again, and it reaches everything in that project.
gandi: Open the settings of your username, then "View my personal access tokens", and choose "Create a token".
Set "Expires in" to 1 year, the longest choice, and replace the token before that date.
Choose "Restrict to selected products", pick your domain, and allow "Manage domain name technical configurations".
Choose "Create" and copy the token; it is shown only once.
digitalocean: Under "Expiration", choose the longest period, and replace the token before it ends.
Choose "Custom Scopes" and select create, read, update and delete for "domain"; a token cannot be limited to one domain.
Choose "Generate Token" and copy it; it is shown only once.
google_cloud: In the project that holds the DNS zone, open "IAM & Admin" > "Service Accounts" and create a service account.
Open the service account, then "Keys" > "Add key" > "Create new key", and choose "JSON".
Paste the whole content of the downloaded file; the project ID is in it, so that field can stay empty.
azure: In "Entra ID" > "App registrations", choose "New registration", then copy the directory (tenant) ID and the application (client) ID.
Open "Certificates & secrets" > "New client secret", choose the longest expiration (at most 24 months), and copy the Value, not the Secret ID.
In the Azure portal, open your DNS zone > "Access control (IAM)" > "Add role assignment" and give the app the "DNS Zone Contributor" role.
Copy the subscription ID and the resource group from the overview of the DNS zone.
Replace the client secret before it expires.
namecom: Open "Account Settings" > "Security" > "API Tokens" and create a production token.
Do not add an IP whitelist, because the node's address can change.
If two-step verification is on, turn on "name.com API Access" at the bottom of the "Security" page.
Fill in your name.com username and the token.
hostinger: Enter a name, choose the longest expiration, and replace the token before that date.
Choose "Generate" and copy the token; it is shown only once and has the same permissions as your user.
desec: Sign in at desec.io and open "Token Management".
Generate a new token and leave "Can create domains" and "Can delete domains" off.
In the advanced settings, leave "Maximum age", "Maximum unused period" and the client subnets empty.
Copy the token; it is shown only once.
inwx: Use a sub-account that can only manage DNS and has no Mobile-TAN, if you can.
Enter the username and password of that account.
If the account uses Mobile-TAN, also enter the shared secret, which is shown only when Mobile-TAN is turned on.
netcup: In the Customer Control Panel, open the domain to see whether it has a "CloudDNS" tab or a "DNS" tab, then open "Master Data" > "API".
CloudDNS tab: choose "Creating an API Key" in "API Keys" and enter only that API key here.
DNS tab: in "Legacy API Keys", choose "Creating an API Key" and then "Regenerating API Password"; the password is shown only once and replaces the one other programs use.
DNS tab: enter the customer number, the Legacy API key and the Legacy API password.
transip: Open the profile icon > "My account" > "API" and turn "Status" on.
Add a key pair and turn "Whitelisted IP" off, because the node's address can change.
Copy the whole private key, including the BEGIN and END lines; it is shown only once.
Fill in the name of your TransIP account.
alidns: In the RAM console, open "Identities" > "Users" > "Create User" and choose access with a permanent AccessKey.
Give the user the custom policy from doc/user/dns-providers/alidns.md in the BuckyOS repository; it allows only your domain.
Copy the AccessKey ID and the AccessKey Secret; the secret is shown only once.
Do not add a network access policy, because the node's address can change.
dnspod: In Tencent Cloud CAM, open "User List" and create a sub-user with programmatic access.
In the DNSPod console, open the domain > "Permission Management" > "CAM permission management" > "add sub-account" and give the sub-user "Full Read/Write".
Open the sub-user in "User List", then "API Key", create a key, and copy the SecretId and SecretKey; the SecretKey is shown only once.
sakura: In the control panel, open "APIキー" in the left menu, choose "APIキーの作成", and select the resource operation type (リソース操作).
Set the access level (アクセスレベル) to "設定編集" (edit settings).
Choose "作成" (create) and copy the access token and the access token secret; the secret is shown only once.
